title: Father's singing, learning horn from Milford Pierron, first job with Bigfoot Phillips
summary: Albert took up singing instead of violin, learned music and horn from Milford Pierron, and took his first job with Bigfoot Phillips. He contrasts the joyful old musicians with today's pay demands.

story.theme_name: First paying gigs: getting started as a young professional
story.community_name: First paid gigs: pay, bands and young beginnings

blocks.x: Yeah, fine. And, well, from there, my daddy was a singer and a violin player. I couldn't stand the violin. I tried it, but that was out of question. So I took up singing, as I told you a lot of times in our interviews. And from there, I went to learn the horn, the music first, and then the horn from Milford Pierron, who was the brother of the violin player. And then after I learned from him how to blow the horn, I got pretty good, and I went to take a job with Bigfoot Phillips. And he told me I learned enough from him, I didn't have to go any further. So that's where I began, that's here in New Orleans. Was there much music in New Orleans that you listened to? Not quite as much as it is now, and it was a different type of day and time in music. In those days, music was played. Well, the guys made a living out of it, but to them it was joy and happiness. And just to get to play the music and make other people happy, that was the aim in these old musicians' lives. Of course, they got paid, but the little Paulson wouldn't have liked to hear the bass of what these guys want today for playing music, which I can agree, it's a living, and it's an artistry, and you should be paid for your artistry, not the condemning of all that. I'm just trying to make a little comparison, as you asked me, in those days and the days now. The music was beautiful because it was what the guys were feeling. It was soulful.
